methods.label: Factor the expression and use primality
methods.explanation:
A prime number cannot be a product of two integers greater than \(1\), so factoring \(f(n)\) can sharply restrict \(n\). To reveal a difference of squares, write
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)&=(n^2+20)^2-(20n)^2\\
&=(n^2+20n+20)(n^2-20n+20).
\end{aligned}
\]
For every positive integer \(n\), the first factor is at least \(41\). The second factor is an integer. If it is nonpositive, the product is not a positive prime; if it is at least \(2\), the product is composite. Thus a prime value requires
\[
n^2-20n+20=1.
\]
Completing the square gives
\[
(n-10)^2=81,
\]
so \(n=1\) or \(n=19\). Both are positive integers, and substitution gives
\[
f(1)=41,\qquad f(19)=761.
\]
We must check that these candidates are prime. A composite integer has a prime divisor no larger than its square root. Both numbers are odd, have digit sums not divisible by \(3\), and do not end in \(0\) or \(5\). Since \(\sqrt{41}<7\), these checks prove that \(41\) is prime. Since \(\sqrt{761}<28\), the remaining primes to check for \(761\) are \(7,11,13,17,19,23\). Division gives remainders \(5,2,7,13,1,2\), respectively, so \(761\) is also prime.

These are the only prime values, and their sum is
\[
41+761=\boxed{802},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
